# A pair-blind source pair with incompatible continuous optimal controls

1 November 2026. Optional complementary construction. This does not replace the inherited path lower bound used for the main interaction-order theorem. The response model and its energy minimum are inherited from pinned Astra N1150/N1152; the five-control source pair and regret argument below are constructed in this investigation.

## Source pair

Let g=e1 and let B have diagonal one, B_(1j)=B_(j1)=3/10 for j=2,3,4,5, B_23=B_32=-4/5, B_45=B_54=4/5, with all other offdiagonal entries zero. Let B' exchange the two dark pairs (2,3) and (4,5), reversing which pair has the negative edge. Both satisfy B>=0, max B_ii=1 and |g_i|<=1.

Proof of PSD: the dark block is the direct sum of two matrices [[1,±4/5],[±4/5,1]], hence positive definite. The scalar Schur complement is

    1-(3/10)^2[2/(1-4/5)+2/(1+4/5)] =0.

The nullspace of B is spanned by

    v=(1,-3/2,-3/2,-1/6,-1/6),

and B' has the two pairs exchanged. In particular each has rank four.

Every complete command using at most two actuators gives identical F for B and B'. If actuator 1 is absent the response is zero; if it is present there is at most one dark actuator, and the relevant 2x2 principal matrix is identical. This covers unlimited precision, arbitrary pair doses and adaptive pair-only measurements.

## Uniform large-dose reduction, with a finite remainder

For dose delta>0 write u=delta*d with d>=0, sum d_i=1. The exact variational representation is

    F_B(delta*d)
      =min_{r:v^T r=1} [(r-g)^T B^+ (r-g)+delta*sum_i d_i r_i^2].

For all strictly positive d, define

    h_v(d)=1/[sum_i v_i^2/d_i],
    r_i^*=(v_i/d_i)/[sum_j v_j^2/d_j].

At a boundary with any d_i=0, set h_v(d)=0; since all v_i are nonzero, a feasible residual supported on that zero coordinate attains zero weighted energy. In all cases,

    delta*h_v(d) <= F_B(delta*d) <= delta*h_v(d)+100.       (1)

For the upper bound, write q_i=v_i r_i^*. These weights are nonnegative and sum to one. Put w_i=e_i/v_i-g. Then r^*-g=sum_i q_i w_i, so convexity of the B^+ quadratic form yields

    (r^*-g)^T B^+(r^*-g) <=max_i w_i^T B^+ w_i=100.

# Simultaneous-intervention lower bound and conventional comparison

1 November 2026. Complementary derivation for the root investigation. All prior Astra source claims below refer only to revision `51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056` of `harjassand/astra-research-knowledge`.

## 1. Contract and notation

We observe scalar values of

    F(u)=g^T P(I+PBP)^(-1)Pg,
    P=diag(sqrt(u)), B>=0,
    |g_i|<=G, B_ii<=kappa,
    u>=0, sum_i u_i<=delta.

Assume delta,kappa,G>0 and write q=delta*kappa and L=delta*G^2. Here L is a global scale, not the actual input energy at a selected command. The experiment order is the support size of the complete actual command. A dense background plus one changed knob counts as dense.

The source representation and accepted determinant theorem are inherited from N1152. Its governing note is `research/2026-10-29-control-acquisition-and-matrix-formulas/source/p1-dark/selection/inference_determinant_tail_theorem.md`. The earlier path construction is `research/2026-10-29-control-acquisition-and-matrix-formulas/source/imports/DARK_INTERVENTION_ORDER.md` (Sections 2--4). That source was retrieved and read in full; its exact text is preserved alongside this note.

## 2. Main lower bound using the inherited path construction

For each integer n>=2 choose g=G(e_1+e_n), B_+=kappa*I+(kappa/4)*A_path, and flip the last offdiagonal edge sign to obtain B_-. Both are strictly positive definite with lower bound kappa/2. All proper-support responses agree at every nonnegative amplitude: the induced forest has at most one bright endpoint in each component, so a diagonal sign gauge can match B_+ to B_- while fixing g.

At u=(delta/n)1, let t=delta/n and a=kappa/4. Their shared determinant D_n obeys

    D_0=1, D_1=1+kappa*t,
    D_j=(1+kappa*t)D_(j-1)-(a*t)^2 D_(j-2).

The inherited cofactor identity gives the exact gap

    Delta_n=4 G^2 a^(n-1) t^n / D_n.

Because tr(t B)=q and B>=0, D_n<=exp(q). Therefore

    Delta_n >= (4L/n) exp(-q) [q/(4n)]^(n-1).       (P)

This quantified-in-n corollary is the useful addition here. The path construction and exact determinant/cofactor gap themselves are already Astra ingredients, and should not be claimed as newly invented.
